chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Louis Armstrong with Fletcher Henderson in New York
summary: Caldwell went to hear Armstrong with Fletcher, who recorded King Porter Stomp; Armstrong stayed about a year then returned to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But I mean now were you in New York when Louie came -- Louie Armstrong played with Fletcher?
Sure. I met Louie when he came off the boat to join Joe Oliver in CHicago.
Right. But you were in New York.
Yeah, when he came to join Fletcher. That's right.
Well, did you go to hear him?

Yeah, he's (unintelligible) with the band, used to go down there. We'd go downstairs (unintelligible) on trombone, and sit up there and listen to him play, and they wrote this thing they recorded, was Jelly Roll's number of "King Porter Stomp." Yeah. (Unintelligible), that was Jelly Johnny.
Well, what -- I mean Louie found that a little (unintelligible), didn't he, as compared to (unintelligible) big Band?
Yes, he did, but he stayed here about a year, then went back to Chicago. That's when he started going for himself, went almost straight up.
